about: Five voters with exactly the same instruction and the same model answer whether a school should ban phones in class, and a tally counts the votes.
how: The five voters work side by side; the tally collects their answers and names the winner.
learns: Voting needs different views. Five copies of one agent give the same answer five times: the vote is unanimous, but it tells you no more than one voter would, and you paid for all five.
watch: The five answers that all start with Yes, and the tally with all five voters in agreement.
